status_values.original: Geometry drawn independently for this app from the topology of the cited reference; no pixels traced or embedded.
status_values.custom: No reliable reference glyph; clearly labeled custom path monogram.

rights: Reference images are Astrodienst Astrowiki (or Wikimedia) material kept outside application assets for study only. The SVG geometry is original work under the project license.

bodies.topology: Key: round orb at the foot, upright stem, K-shaped arms opening to the right from one junction. Stem offset left so the orb and arms balance around the center. The 1-pixel stub under the reference orb is not drawn; the larger Asteroid List glyph (Symbol-chi-big.gif) ends the stem at the orb.

bodies.identity: Mean lunar apogee (Swiss Ephemeris MEAN_APOG), not asteroid 1181 Lilith.

reference.note: Article "Symbol" image is a filled crescent, horns to the left. Astrodienst chart drawings (Radix_Eros_Fotonachweis.gif) draw Lilith as a dark crescent over a cross.

bodies.topology: Filled crescent, horns to the left, above a cross. The cross keeps it distinct from a plain Moon crescent.

reference.note: Article: "The glyph for Ceres represents the sickle".

bodies.topology: Sickle hook opening to the lower left, returning to a stem with a crossbar.
Diamond on a stem with a crossbar; the lower vertex of the diamond starts the stem.

reference.note: Article "Symbol" image; footnote: scepter topped with a star. The Asteroid List also shows a star-over-circle variant (Juno2.png), not used.

bodies.topology: Eight-ray star whose vertical ray continues as the scepter stem, with a crossbar.

reference.note: Article "Symbol" image. The Asteroid List also shows a curled-flame variant (Vesta.png) and an altar variant (Vesta2.png), not used.

bodies.topology: Vertical flame line inside a small V, nested in a larger V with horizontal rim wings.

reference.note: The article shows only a "Symbol proposal on Wikipedia" by one user (2013). Astrodienst chart drawings label the body "433 Eros" with no glyph (Radix_Eros_Fotonachweis.gif).

bodies.topology: Custom path monogram "Er" (the body abbreviation), mono-line strokes. No reliable Astrodienst glyph exists and the proposal is not adopted by Astrodienst charts, so no symbol is invented.

reference.note: Article "Symbol" image (the plain Psyche page has no text). Footnote: star and butterfly wings.

bodies.topology: Six-ray star (horizontal bar and two diagonals) above a closed arch with a flat base.
Centaur family: wide flat ellipse, centered stem, closed P bowl to the right at the top.
Centaur family: wide flat ellipse, centered stem forming the left leg of an N whose diagonal falls to a right leg. Open zigzag versus the closed Pholus bowl.
